title: Zero‑Trust Incident Evidence Handbook
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose
This handbook defines a single, auditable evidence workflow for security incidents in zero‑trust and multi‑tenant contexts. It ties RBAC decisions, audit logs, data residency restrictions, and SDLC controls to a reproducible incident response procedure so security, legal, and customers can independently validate remediation and regulatory artifacts.

Scope
- Applies to incidents that impact confidentiality, integrity, or availability of tenant data or control plane services.
- Covers evidence collection, packaging, retention mapping, access controls for evidence, and sign‑off cadence.
- Not intended for routine operational alerts (handled by oncall runbooks) unless they escalate to an incident.

Audience
Security engineers, incident commanders, SRE oncall, legal/compliance leads, support escalation engineers, and platform product managers.

Key Principles
- Least privilege: evidence access follows RBAC and JIT privilege activation; no broad evidence buckets.
- Immutable sources: use append‑only audit exports and content hashing for chain‑of‑custody.
- Region‑aware packaging: evidence containing PII or regionally regulated telemetry must follow data residency rules when exported.
- Reproducibility: every artifact contains the query, time window, and tool version used to create it.

Owner & Critical Services
- Incident owner: Security Incident Response (SIR) team. Primary contact: Elena Martinez (Security PM).
- Critical services in scope: auth-api (internal), audit-streamer, telemetry-ingest, kv-cache, model-serving-proxy.
- Evidence store: secure-evidence-bucket (S3, KMS encrypted), immutable-audit-store (time-series archive), forensics-host (air‑gapped VM snapshots).

Roles & Responsibilities (table)
- Responders and signers:
| Role | Team | Responsibility | Escalation threshold |
| Incident Commander (IC) | security | Coordinates response, approves evidence release | Sev2 or above |
| Forensic Lead | security | Runs audit queries, exports chain-of-custody | Any suspected data exfil |
| SRE Liaison | eng-sre | Collects system snapshots, CPU/memory traces | Service-level degradation > 10% |
| Legal/Compliance | finance-legal | Advises on disclosure and retention | Data subject request or regulator notice |
| Customer Success | customer-success | Coordinates outbound comms if customer impacted | Confirmed tenant data exposure |

Minimum SLOs for Evidence Package
- Time to initial evidence snapshot: 60 minutes from incident declaration.
- Proof of collection: SHA256 hash and signed manifest within 90 minutes.
- Evidence access provisioning: 15 minutes for JIT approvals for named reviewers.

Incident Evidence Workflow (step-by-step)
1) Incident declaration
   - IC creates the incident ticket and tags it with data sensitivity: {none, low, high, regulated}.
   - If regulated, immediately notify Legal and set package-residency flag.
2) Lockdown & preserve ephemeral state
   - SRE runs snapshot commands and captures process lists, network state, and container IDs. Example CLI snippet:
     - ssh forensics@forensics-host -- sudo ./capture_snapshot.sh --incident $INCIDENT_ID --services "auth-api,audit-streamer"
3) RBAC evidence collection
   - Export role changes and sign-in events for the 72h window prior to incident:
     - audit-query: SELECT * FROM auth_events WHERE (event_type IN ('role_grant','role_revoke','login')) AND ts BETWEEN $T0 AND $T1;
   - Include policy versions and role‑assignment manifests.
4) Audit log extraction
   - Pull immutable-audit-store segments covering the incident window and associated trace IDs.
   - Preserve both raw message stream (gzipped) and a parsed summary (CSV) used for triage.
5) Data residency filter
   - If package-residency=EU, copy artifacts only to eu-evidence-bucket (replication disabled) and log the transfer with KMS key id.
6) Secure packaging & manifest
   - Create manifest.json (required fields: incident_id, created_by, tool_versions, time_window, sha256 list). Example manifest line: {"path":"/evidence/2026-02-02/auth-events-1.gz","sha256":"...","size":"12345"}
   - Sign manifest with k8s-signing-key: kubectl exec signer -- /opt/sign-manifest --manifest manifest.json --key-id evidence-signing-v1
7) Chain-of-custody recording
   - Append manifest entry to chain-of-custody ledger in immutable-audit-store with signature and timestamp.
8) Evidence access control
   - Create a temporary RBAC grant for reviewer group: evidence-reviewers.$INCIDENT_ID with expiry 48 hours. Use JIT activation and require MFA.
9) Review, redact, and release
   - Legal performs PII review and indicates fields requiring redaction. For regulated incidents, an independent auditor must sign off before external disclosure.
10) Archive & retention declaration
   - Archive final package to long-term store with retention labels: retention=incident-class-X (see retention table below).

Evidence Packaging Checklist (required)
- [x] manifest.json signed (signature and public key id)
- [x] audit-store segment (raw) with sha256
- [x] parsed CSV of key events used in investigation
- [x] RBAC dump (policy versions + diffs)
- [x] System snapshot (sha256) and list of hostnames
- [x] Chain-of-custody ledger entry id
- [x] Redaction map (if any) and redaction justification
- [x] Evidence access list and expiry timestamps

Retention Mapping (table)
- retention rules are applied at packaging time and encoded into object metadata.
| Incident class | Retention label | Minimum retention | Access review cadence |
| PII exposure - regulated | incident-class-H | 7 years (or regulator-required) | annual |
| PII exposure - non-regulated | incident-class-M | 3 years | biennial |
| No customer data | incident-class-L | 12 months | biennial |

RBAC & JIT Controls
- Evidence store policy: only evidence-service principal and signer role can write to secure-evidence-bucket.
- Reviewer access is provisioned via evidence-reviewers.$INCIDENT_ID temporary group and enforced by attribute-based conditions: requester.department in {security,legal,compliance} AND request.context.mfa = true.
- JIT activation flow: request -> manager approval (within 15 min) -> IAM issues short token (TTL 48h) -> IAM logs activation to audit-streamer.

Audit Logging & Queries (examples)
- Immutable audit export command (internal tool):
  ./audit-export --service auth-api --from $T0 --to $T1 --format gz --out /tmp/$INCIDENT_ID/auth-audit.gz
- Example quick triage query (SQL on parsed CSV index):
  SELECT user_id, action, ip, ts FROM parsed_audit WHERE trace_id = 'TRACE-1234' ORDER BY ts ASC LIMIT 500;
- Key thresholds to surface in evidence package:
  - Unsuccessful login rate spike: > 5x baseline over 10 minutes
  - Role grant anomalies: any grant where source != automation-bot AND approver IS NULL

Secure SDLC Evidence Linkages
- If the incident traces to a code change, include the following with the package:
  - PR id and merge commit hash
  - Build artifact digest and provenance (CI job id, runner id, environment variables snapshot)
  - Feature flag state during deployment and rollout percentage
- Required attestation: release owner must attest to canary metrics and rollback actions in the incident ticket.

Risk & Exceptions Process
- Risk classification: every incident is assigned a risk score (0–100) by the IC using the scoring rubric attached. High risk (score >= 70) requires board notification and an external auditor engagement.
- Exceptions and evidence withholding:
  - Temporary exceptions to residency can be approved by Legal + CISO only, with compensating controls documented and evidence labeled: "exception-approved-$ID".
  - All exceptions are timeboxed and must include a mitigation roadmap.

Communication & Disclosure
- Internal communication lanes: #incidents (ops), #sec-briefing (security), private channel with Legal.
- Customer notification triggers: confirmed tenant data exposure OR SLA-blind impact. Draft notice template is appended to every incident package and must include the manifest id and access url.

Forensics & Long‑term Validation
- Periodic revalidation: archived packages with incident-class-H are rehashed and validated annually; mismatches trigger re‑ingestion.
- Independent audit: for regulated incidents, we keep an auditor read-only snapshot for 3 years and log every auditor access event in immutable-audit-store.

Appendix A — Incident Scoring Rubric (summary)
- Confidentiality impact: 0–40 points (based on data types exposed)
- Availability impact: 0–30 points (user-facing outages)
- Integrity impact: 0–20 points (model or config tampering)
- Likelihood/velocity: 0–10 points (attack automation, exploitation speed)

Appendix B — Example manifest.json (trimmed)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0142",
  "created_by": "elena.martinez",
  "time_window": "2026-02-02T02:14:00Z/2026-02-02T03:01:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    {"path": "/evidence/INC-2026-0142/auth-audit-1.gz", "sha256": "abc123...", "size": "1,024,000"}
  ],
  "signed_by": "evidence-signing-v1",
  "signature": "MEUCIQ..."
}
